meta.description: Free calorie deficit calculator: estimate your maintenance calories (TDEE) and the daily intake for a 250–1,000 kcal deficit. Metric or imperial units.

lead: Estimate your maintenance calories, then see the daily intake that a deficit of 250 to 1,000 kcal leaves.
form.label: Calorie deficit calculator
err.age: Enter an age from 18 to 120 years. This calculator is for adults.
result.floor: That is under 1,200 kcal a day. A smaller deficit is easier to keep up, or check with a doctor or a dietitian first.
table.caption: Daily intake by deficit at your activity level
result.note: An estimate, not a measurement or a plan. Not for pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to a doctor or a registered dietitian before a big change to your diet.
method.p1: A calorie deficit means eating fewer calories than your body uses. The calculator first estimates your maintenance calories (TDEE): your BMR from the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, multiplied by an activity factor.
method.p2: Activity factors: 1.2 sedentary, 1.375 lightly active, 1.55 moderately active, 1.725 very active, 1.9 extra active. Then the calculator subtracts the deficit you choose. The options stop at 1,000 kcal a day and any intake under 1,200 kcal a day is flagged: the same limits Calcalou uses, based on the NHLBI clinical guidelines.
method.source: Sources: Mifflin MD, St Jeor ST et al. A new predictive equation for resting energy expenditure in healthy individuals. Am J Clin Nutr. 1990;51(2):241–247. NHLBI. Clinical Guidelines on the Identification, Evaluation, and Treatment of Overweight and Obesity in Adults. 1998.
app.title: Set a deficit goal in Calcalou
app.text: In Calcalou you can set a daily deficit as your goal. The app limits it to 1,000 kcal, warns when your base burn minus the deficit leaves under 1,200 kcal, and shows eaten against burned, with your base burn and the activity you log, so you see what's left for today.
faq.deficit.a: A calorie deficit means eating fewer calories than your body burns in a day. This calculator estimates the burn side, your TDEE, and subtracts the deficit you pick.
faq.maintenance.a: Maintenance calories, or TDEE, are the estimated calories that keep your weight about the same: your BMR plus everyday movement and exercise.
faq.size.q: How big a deficit does this calculator allow?
faq.size.a: From 250 to 1,000 kcal a day. Calcalou uses the same 1,000 kcal limit, based on the NHLBI clinical guidelines. Plan a bigger change with a doctor or a dietitian.
faq.floor.q: Why is an intake under 1,200 kcal flagged?
faq.floor.a: In the NHLBI guidelines, 1,200 kcal a day is the top of the low-calorie range for women and the bottom of the range for men. The calculator does not know your situation, so it flags any intake under 1,200 kcal instead of suggesting it.
